title: Etale projective neighborhoods of a flat finitely presented algebra
statement: Let $R\to S$ be a flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] homomorphism of commutative rings of finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. Let $\mathfrak q\subset S$ be a prime with inverse image $\mathfrak p\subset R$. There are commutative rings $R^{\prime},S^{\prime}$, ring maps forming a commutative square $R\to S$, $R\to R^{\prime}$, $S\to S^{\prime}$, $R^{\prime}\to S^{\prime}$, and primes $\mathfrak q^{\prime}\subset S^{\prime}$, $\mathfrak p^{\prime}\subset R^{\prime}$, such that: (1) the horizontal neighborhood maps $R\to R^{\prime}$ and $S\to S^{\prime}$ have etale spectrum maps [def-weil-etale-morphism]; (2) $\mathfrak q^{\prime}$ contracts to $\mathfrak q$ and $\mathfrak p^{\prime}$, and $\mathfrak p^{\prime}$ contracts to $\mathfrak p$; (3) their induced residue-field maps $\kappa(\mathfrak p)\to\kappa(\mathfrak p^{\prime})$ and $\kappa(\mathfrak q)\to\kappa(\mathfrak q^{\prime})$ are isomorphisms; (4) $S^{\prime}$ is a finitely presented $R^{\prime}$-algebra and a projective $R^{\prime}$-module [def-weil-pbc-projective-module]. In addition the induced homomorphism $C=S\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)\to C^{\prime}=S^{\prime}\otimes_{R^{\prime}}\kappa(\mathfrak p^{\prime})$ has etale spectrum map and takes the fibre prime corresponding to $\mathfrak q^{\prime}$ to that corresponding to $\mathfrak q$ by inverse image [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-primes-bijection]. Residue fields and tensor products are [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime, def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. No finite-generation assumption over $R^{\prime}$ is made for the projective module $S^{\prime}$.

source.place: Tag 05ID, proposition-finite-presentation-flat-at-point, specialized to the structure sheaf on Spec S; the induced etale fibre map is the diagram used in Tag 05IG, lemma-weak-bourbaki-pre, first proof paragraph. In that paragraph the printed kappa(q-prime) in the definition of the fibre ring is corrected to kappa(p-prime).

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-complete-algebra-devissage-etale-existence] to $N=S$. A finite algebra presentation makes $S$ finitely generated as an $R$-algebra, and $1$ generates $S$ as an $S$-module. Obtain $R_0,S_0,\mathfrak p_0,\mathfrak q_0$ and the pointed etale square with the stated residue-field isomorphisms. Under the explicit isomorphism $S\otimes_SS_0\to S_0$, $s\otimes t\mapsto st$ (inverse $t\mapsto1\otimes t$), its complete devissage is one of $S_0/S_0/R_0$ over $\mathfrak p_0$. No assertion about projectivity has yet been used.

source.place: Tag 05ID, proposition-finite-presentation-flat-at-point, apply existence of complete devissage; Tag 05I1 algebraic form

proof.text: Put $T=S\otimes_RR_0$ and let $h:T\to S_0$, $s\otimes a\mapsto s a$, be induced by the commutative square. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], $\operatorname{Spec}T=\operatorname{Spec}S\times_{\operatorname{Spec}R}\operatorname{Spec}R_0$. Its projection to $\operatorname{Spec}S$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change]. The composite of $\operatorname{Spec}h$ with this projection is the given etale map $\operatorname{Spec}S_0\to\operatorname{Spec}S$. Hence cancellation in [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation], clause (3), shows that $\operatorname{Spec}h$ is etale. This does not require the original square to be cartesian.

source.place: Tag 05B8, lemma-etale-at-point, proof: etale morphism to the base change

proof.text: Since $\operatorname{Spec}h$ is etale, it is locally of finite presentation by [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Both spectra are affine, so [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation], applied to the whole source and target, makes $T\to S_0$ finitely presented. The base-change part of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-base-change-composition] makes $R_0\to T$ finitely presented from the given $R\to S$. Its composition part therefore gives that $R_0\to S_0$ is finitely presented.

source.place: Tag 05ID, finite-presentation hypotheses on the resulting affine diagram; etale permanence and affine finite presentation

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map-iff-flat-affine], the assumed flatness of $R\to S$ makes $\operatorname{Spec}S\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ flat. Its base change $\operatorname{Spec}T\to\operatorname{Spec}R_0$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change]; the same affine equivalence gives flatness of $R_0\to T$. The etaleness of $\operatorname{Spec}h$ gives flatness of $T\to S_0$ by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-flat]. Composition by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map-comp] proves that $S_0$ is flat as an $R_0$-module. Thus flatness over the new base has been checked, not inferred merely from the commutative square.

source.place: Tag 05ID, flatness over the new etale base (the source uses Tag 05B9; here use the etale map to the cartesian base change)

proof.text: The module $S_0$ is finitely presented over itself: take the presentation $S_0^0\to S_0\xrightarrow{1}S_0\to0$. Apply [lem-trf-complete-algebra-devissage-projective-localization] to $R_0\to S_0$, $N=S_0$, and $\mathfrak r=\mathfrak p_0$. Its algebra finite-presentation hypothesis is Step 3, its module flatness hypothesis is Step 4, and its complete-devissage hypothesis is Step 1. Obtain $f\in R_0\setminus\mathfrak p_0$ such that $(S_0)_f$ is projective over $(R_0)_f$. Set $R^{\prime}=(R_0)_f$ and $S^{\prime}=(S_0)_f$. The fraction map $S_0\otimes_{R_0}(R_0)_f\to(S_0)_f$, $b\otimes(a/f^k)\mapsto ab/f^k$, with inverse $b/f^k\mapsto b\otimes1/f^k$, identifies these definitions. By [lem-trf-localization-finite-presentation-ring-map], $S^{\prime}$ remains finitely presented as an $R^{\prime}$-algebra.

source.place: Tag 05ID, last sentence; Tag 05IB, projectivity after a standard open of the base

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-principal-localization-open-immersion], the spectra of $R^{\prime}$ and $S^{\prime}$ are the standard opens $D(f)$ of $\operatorname{Spec}R_0$ and $\operatorname{Spec}S_0$: inverse image sends a prime in a localization to a prime avoiding $f$, with inverse $\mathfrak a\mapsto\{b/f^k:b\in\mathfrak a\}$. The cited node supplies the open immersions; hence etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation], clause (1); composing with the original etale neighbourhood maps, using clause (2), proves (1). As $f\notin\mathfrak p_0$ and $\mathfrak q_0\cap R_0=\mathfrak p_0$, both primes avoid $f$. Define $\mathfrak p^{\prime}=\mathfrak p_0(R_0)_f$ and $\mathfrak q^{\prime}=\mathfrak q_0(S_0)_f$. Clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-prime-residue-field-iso] gives all contractions in (2), and its clauses (2)--(3) identify the local rings and residue fields. Explicitly: Localizing these rings at the marked primes gives the original local rings: inverting $f$ first adds no denominators since $f$ is already outside the prime. The maps $a/s\mapsto(a/1)/(s/1)$ and $(a/f^k)/(b/f^l)\mapsto af^l/(bf^k)$ are inverse. Passing to residue fields therefore adds only isomorphisms to the isomorphisms of Step 1, proving (3). Together with Step 5 this proves all four neighbourhood clauses.

source.place: Tag 05ID, final standard-open replacement; fraction descriptions of primes and local rings

proof.text: Apply the construction in Step 2 to the final square. Its horizontal maps are etale by Step 6; thus $\operatorname{Spec}S^{\prime}\to\operatorname{Spec}(S\otimes_RR^{\prime})$ is etale by the same cancellation argument. Base change along $R^{\prime}\to\kappa(\mathfrak p^{\prime})$ preserves this by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change]. Using [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], the resulting ring map is $S\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p^{\prime})\to S^{\prime}\otimes_{R^{\prime}}\kappa(\mathfrak p^{\prime})$. If $\iota:\kappa(\mathfrak p)\xrightarrow{\sim}\kappa(\mathfrak p^{\prime})$ is Step 6's isomorphism, then $s\otimes\lambda\mapsto s\otimes\iota(\lambda)$, with inverse induced by $\iota^{-1}$, identifies its source with $C$. Tensor reassociation here is given by $(s\otimes a)\otimes t\mapsto s\otimes at$, inverse $s\otimes t\mapsto(s\otimes1)\otimes t$. Thus the induced map $C\to C^{\prime}$ has etale spectrum map as required.

source.place: Tag 05IG, first paragraph, etale map between the fibre rings; Tag 05B8 proof

proof.text: Let $j:S\to C$ and $j^{\prime}:S^{\prime}\to C^{\prime}$ be the maps $b\mapsto b\otimes1$, and let $u:C\to C^{\prime}$ be Step 7's map. Let $\mathfrak Q^{\prime}\subset C^{\prime}$ be the prime corresponding to $\mathfrak q^{\prime}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-primes-bijection], $(j^{\prime})^{-1}(\mathfrak Q^{\prime})=\mathfrak q^{\prime}$. The equality $u j=j^{\prime}(S\to S^{\prime})$, checked on $b$, implies $j^{-1}(u^{-1}\mathfrak Q^{\prime})=\mathfrak q$ by Step 6's contraction. The bijection in the same cited node identifies the unique prime of $C$ with contraction $\mathfrak q$ as the fibre prime corresponding to $\mathfrak q$. Hence $u^{-1}\mathfrak Q^{\prime}$ is exactly that prime, which proves the last assertion.

source.place: Tag 05IG, fibre-prime correspondence in the first paragraph (with kappa(p-prime) in the second fibre ring)
